- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a 1-2 day lag correction.
- In early horizon (e.g., 30d forecast), model often fails to capture mean reversion toward 65–75 range; cap forecasts at ±3σ from recent 10-day average.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model tends to hold high forecasts; reduce forecast slope by 10–15% in second half of horizon.
- Avoid overreacting to single-day sentiment spikes; smooth sentiment transitions before adjusting forecast weights.
